pins.name: RUN
pins.description: RP2040 enable, pulled up inside (~50 kΩ): short to ground to reset

pins.name: AGND
pins.description: analog ground for GP26-28 (join to GND when the ADC is not critical)

pins.name: ADC_VREF
pins.description: the ADC's reference, filtered 3.3 V on the board

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: 3V3(OUT): the board's 3.3 V regulator output, keep loads under 300 mA

pins.name: 3V3_EN
pins.description: the regulator's enable, pulled up to VSYS (100 kΩ): short to ground to switch 3.3 V off

pins.name: VSYS
pins.description: the system supply, 1.8-5.5 V: from VBUS through a Schottky diode, or feed it here (through a diode when USB is used too)

pins.name: VBUS
pins.description: USB 5 V when the USB cable is plugged in (0 V otherwise)

notes: Same header pinout and footprint as the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 (RASPBERRY_PI_PICO_2); GPIOs are 3.3 V. The RP2350B's extra GPIOs (30-47) stay on the module: GPIO47 is the PSRAM's chip select, the BOOT button doubles as a user input. In PCBKit 3V3 is `P3V3`, 3V3_EN `P3V3_EN`.

Runs firmware in PCBKit's RP2350 model (RISC-V cores): flash images with an IMAGE_DEF, flashed as a UF2 (family rp2350_riscv) onto the BOOTSEL drive; build with the rp2350 kit and name the program folder with `firmware` on the component.
Early stock uses RP2350 A2 (erratum RP2350-E9: an input with its internal pull-down can latch high; use pull-ups or external pull-downs of 8.2 kΩ or less).

pins.source: Pimoroni Pico Plus 2 product page (Pico pinout, PSRAM on GPIO47) and the Raspberry Pi Pico 2 pinout it shares
